grade.primary_choice: Separate Node.js/TypeScript worker service on Fly.io fed by the existing Redis queue
unsupported_claims: 'Enqueuing directly after commit can... deliver ones that rolled back' is wrong: enqueuing after commit can lose events, but only enqueuing before commit can deliver rolled-back ones
'The bill will mostly come from Postgres and Redis storage' is stated as fact without support
grade.notes: A clear Node recommendation backed by correct Little's-law sizing, with Go kept as a measured fallback and buy-versus-build treated as a real option. It covers nearly every must-mention point; the only gaps are Redis AOF persistence, restricting redirects and ports for SSRF, and not stating outright that each (event, endpoint) pair is its own job.
